title: Conscious possession - the most litigated phrase in NDPS cases
p1:
A person is found near drugs. Is that enough to prove guilt?

Not always. In NDPS cases, one phrase often decides the entire battle: “conscious possession.”
p2:
Many believe that simply being close to a banned substance means automatic liability. The surprising part is that the law looks beyond physical presence. Courts examine whether the person knew about the substance and had control over it.

A bag, vehicle, or room containing contraband may create questions, but knowledge and control are often the real issues argued in court.
p3:
This is why “conscious possession” has become one of the most debated concepts in NDPS litigation. A person’s connection with the substance, awareness of its presence, and ability to exercise control can change the outcome of a case.

The practical takeaway: possession in law is not always about who is physically closest to an object. The surrounding facts matter.
conclusion: Do you think being found near illegal substances should be enough for conviction, or should knowledge and control always be proved?
